CHIEF COMPLAINT
Annual examination.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
56-year-old female with past medical history of coronary artery disease, prior stenting, prior carpal tunnel release, and herniated disc who presents for annual examination. Patient reports that her herniated disc has been doing well since a steroid injection several months ago, with no back pain or limitations in movement. Regarding her prior carpal tunnel release, she reports that she is back to work without any issues, has full range of motion, and denies numbness or tingling in her hands. Regarding her coronary artery disease and prior stenting, patient reports experiencing chest pain over the past month. She describes the pain as a burning sensation located in the middle of her chest. The pain occurs with exertion, particularly when walking, and resolves with rest. She does not experience chest pain at rest. She experiences this pain approximately three times per week. She denies associated shortness of breath, nausea, or vomiting. Patient also reports mild nasal congestion from allergies.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies shortness of breath, nausea, vomiting, lower extremity edema, muscle aches, fever, and chills. Endorses chest pain with exertion and nasal congestion from allergies.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Coronary artery disease
Prior stenting
Prior carpal tunnel release
Herniated disc

MEDICATIONS
Aspirin
Toprol

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient is currently employed and working.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Blood pressure well-controlled. Oxygen saturation normal.
Heart: Slight 3/6 systolic ejection murmur.
Lungs: Clear.
Neck: No carotid bruits appreciated.
Extremities: No lower extremity edema. Healed surgical scars noted on right wrist.

RESULTS
Echocardiogram from prior year: Left ventricular ejection fraction 45%. Mitral regurgitation noted.
EKG: Stable, consistent with prior coronary artery disease. No new changes.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Carpal tunnel release: Patient reports good recovery with return to work and no recurrent symptoms. No further intervention needed at this time. Patient instructed to report if recurrent symptoms develop.
2. Herniated disc: Patient reports improvement since prior steroid injection with no pain or movement limitations. No further steroid injection or physical therapy indicated at this time. Patient instructed to report if recurrent symptoms develop.
3. Coronary artery disease with chest pain: Continue aspirin and toprol. Cardiac stress test ordered. Lipid panel ordered. Crestor 20 mg once daily initiated.
